category_title: Students with learning difficulties and attention issues who reset tasks when challenged
minimal_context: The student is practicing single-digit addition, subtraction, and multiplication sums in the x20 game on a Nintendo DS.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please open the x20 game on the Nintendo DS and start solving the addition and subtraction sums.

STUDENT: (Looks at the screen and appears bored) I can read the sums, but I don't know how to do these calculations.

TUTOR: Just keep trying to answer the next one.

STUDENT: (Looks away from the screen, easily distracted) This sum is getting too challenging. If I don't get it right, I won't get the highest score.

TUTOR: What do you think the answer might be?

STUDENT: (Reaches for the console and resets the Nintendo DS) It's too hard to complete. I'm restarting the game because I'm not going to do well on this one.

options.A: Use verbal redirects and reflective statements to sustain and maintain the student's game interaction.
options.B: Make explicit moves acknowledging and praising appropriate student behaviors during the Nintendo DS game.
options.C: Provide concrete aids including rulers and number lines, and encourage finger counting for the sums.
options.D: Ignore the student's behavior of resetting the Nintendo DS console, where safe to do so.
